claims.statement: The corpus is synthetic rather than a real carrier product, ISO form, or legal advice, and it separates frozen forms and regulator bulletins from living internal guidelines that are revised in place.

HO-3 2018-09 applicability statement supersedes the HO-3 2011-05 edition for policies written on or after 2018-09-01, while HO-3 2011-05 remains in force for policies written under it regardless of when a loss is reported.
HO 01 45 is a Texas amendment attached to HO-3 for policies effective on or after 2022-01-01 and governs when it conflicts with the attached HO-3 form.
Internal claims guidance is not part of any policy and must not be quoted to an insured or claimant; it directs staff to establish and document the water source before evaluating damage.
A state-specific appetite guide may impose tighter limits than the enterprise referral matrix but may not grant broader authority, and a referral cannot approve a state filing or bulletin violation.
HO 04 90 editions 2010-10 and 2026-01 W.1 write back the stated HO-3 Section I A.3 sewer/drain-backup and sump-event exclusion when the endorsement is verified attached.
HO 04 81 M.1 writes back HO-3 2018-09 Section I Exclusions C.2 only for fungi, rot, or bacteria resulting from a Section I insured peril during the policy period.

Texas Bulletin B-2021-08 applies to Texas residential property policies delivered or issued for delivery with effective dates on or after 2022-01-01 and establishes regulatory requirements for separate windstorm/hail deductibles, including nonstacking on the same wind/hail loss.

Florida Bulletin OIR-2023-04 applies to Florida personal residential property policies issued or renewed with effective dates on or after 2023-07-01 and governs roof-age decisions, inspection, roof-deductible or ACV-schedule offers, nonrenewal, deductible nonstacking, and reporting.

Under the internal referral matrix, referral and management approval are escalation mechanisms, whereas conditions outside appetite or conflicting with a filing or bulletin cannot be cleared by referral and must not be bound.

Under HO-3 2018-09, Coverage A and B property follows the direct-physical-loss grant subject to Section I exclusions, while Coverage C requires direct physical loss caused by one of P.2's listed perils; neither path bypasses applicable exclusions or a verified endorsement's limits.
HO 04 90 W.4 preserves HO-3 2018-09 Section I Exclusions A.1 and A.2, so the water-backup endorsement does not restore flood, surface-water, or subsurface-water loss.
HO 04 16 O.1 writes back HO-3 2018-09 Section I Exclusions D.1 for the stated covered-loss ordinance-or-law cost.
HO 23 74 R.1-R.2 modifies HO-3 2018-09 Section I A.4 only for windstorm- or hail-caused roof-surfacing settlement.
HO 23 74 R.6 preserves HO-3 2018-09 Section I Exclusions D.1 for ordinance-required replacement of undamaged roof surfacing; the roof-schedule endorsement does not itself pay that cost.
HO 01 45 T.1 modifies HO-3 2018-09 Section I Conditions S.5 so that, for windstorm or hail loss, only the separate windstorm-and-hail deductible applies under the attached amendment's terms.
HO 01 45 T.1 implements Texas Bulletin B-2021-08 B.3's windstorm-and-hail deductible application and mixed-peril allocation rule.

HO 04 90 2010-10 remains in force for policies written under it, while 2026-01 replaces it for policies written on or after 2026-01-01 and remains in force for policies written under it; 2027-01 replaces 2026-01 for policies written on or after 2027-01-01.

The HO 04 90 editions have distinct default payment mechanics: 2010-10 sets a $5,000 policy-period sublimit and $500 separate deductible, while 2026-01 sets a $10,000 sublimit and $1,000 separate deductible; each sublimit is within A/B/C limits and each separate deductible displaces the Section I deductible for covered endorsement loss.

HO 04 90 2026-01 and 2027-01 W.6 condition water-backup coverage for a residence with finished area below grade on an installed and operable at-loss backwater valve or equivalent device on the serving sewer line; 2026-01 identifies the requirement as new relative to 2010-10.
Both HO 04 90 editions preserve the HO-3 flood/surface-water and subsurface-water exclusions through W.4, so their A.3 write-back is not flood coverage.

Both HO 04 90 editions withhold endorsement coverage when the backup, overflow, or discharge resulted from the insured's known pre-loss failure to maintain the serving sewer line, drain, sump, or sump pump and a reasonable person would have remedied it.

Florida H.4 and Texas G.3 use a battery-backed sump pump as a pre-bind internal control for a requested HO 04 90 limit above $10,000 and finished below-grade area, whereas 2026-01 W.6 is a distinct at-loss serving-sewer backflow-device coverage condition with no stated limit threshold.

HO 04 90 2027-01 W.2-W.3 sets a $10,000 policy-period default sublimit unless a higher endorsement Declarations limit is shown, treats that sublimit as within A/B/C limits, and applies a separate $1,000 deductible instead of the Section I deductible for covered endorsement loss.

HO 04 90 2027-01 W.1 writes back the stated HO-3 Section I A.3 sewer/drain-backup and sump-event exclusion when the endorsement is verified attached, while W.4 preserves the HO-3 A.1 flood/surface-water and A.2 subsurface-water exclusions.
